section: The sources to walk
title: Walk every one of these, in this order, and give each item a row: initial_spec.md 2.1, 4, 5, 8.8, 9, map Decisions so far, map Constraints, CONTEXT.md

section: The sources to walk
title: CONTEXT.md terms are kept only when the specification depends on the term; a term that exists to explain the code records `refused` with `note` naming the internal vocabulary it describes

section: The sources to walk
title: The map's `## Non-goals` need no rows: they are refusals that the specification already carries, and each becomes the `refused` disposition of the requirement it belongs to

section: How to fill each row
title: `title`: one line, the requirement in the source's own words where they are already short, otherwise a faithful compression; never a paraphrase that widens or narrows the meaning

section: How to fill each row
title: `source`: `initial_spec.md §4.12`, `map.md ## Decisions so far #14`, `CONTEXT.md . Leave time`

section: How to fill each row
title: `status`: `kept`, `superseded`, `duplicate`, `refused`, or `deferred`

section: How to fill each row
title: `target`: for `superseded`, the identifier that replaces it; for `duplicate`, the canonical identifier; empty otherwise

section: How to fill each row
title: `effort`: for `kept` rows only, the child effort slug that owes it, chosen from the settled twelve; a row that no effort owes is a row that is not `kept`

section: How to fill each row
title: `spec`: leave empty; `to-spec` fills it when it writes the specification

section: How to fill each row
title: `note`: the reason for `refused` and `deferred`, and anything a reader needs to follow `superseded` and `duplicate`; empty otherwise

section: How to fill each row
title: A `deferred` row names `v2` in `note` and nothing else in the row pretends it is scheduled
